cve_candidates.description: Default 'public' read and 'private' write community strings enable full MIB tree walk (system info, interfaces, routing, processes) and unauthenticated configuration modification.
SNMP UDP amplification vector — bulk GET responses significantly larger than requests, enabling DoS amplification.
NTP monlist command returns up to 600 last clients — ~206x amplification factor and leaks internal client IP addresses.
Multiple stack-based buffer overflows in ntpd allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via crafted packets.
Path traversal vulnerability in tftpd-hpa allows attackers to read files outside the TFTP root directory using ../ sequences.
TFTP provides no authentication by protocol design — misconfigured servers allow unauthenticated arbitrary file read (/etc/passwd, SSH keys, configs) and write (web shells, cron jobs).
Avahi daemon local denial-of-service and information disclosure via crafted mDNS packets.
Avahi responds to unicast queries with multicast responses, enabling DNS amplification/traffic amplification attacks.
Heap-based buffer overflow in rsyslog when receiving malformed UDP syslog messages, potentially leading to remote code execution.
Unauthenticated RIPv1 route injection on UDP/520 — attacker can inject false routes to perform man-in-the-middle or traffic hijacking attacks on the local subnet.
IPMI 2.0 RAKP authentication flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain HMAC-SHA1 password hashes without completing authentication, enabling offline brute-force.
CoAP (UDP/5683) is an unauthenticated IoT protocol — potential amplification vector and information disclosure of device resources without authentication.

attack_surface_summary: The target (172.19.0.2, hostname: redteam_easy-target-1.redteam_easy_engagement-net) exposes zero TCP services — all 65,535 TCP ports returned RST, indicating either a host-based firewall blocking all TCP inbound or no running TCP daemons. The attack surface is exclusively UDP-based, with 16 ports returning open|filtered state across highly sensitive protocols: SNMP (UDP/161) is the highest-priority target due to default community strings ('public'/'private') enabling unauthenticated full MIB enumeration and potential write-access for configuration tampering. TFTP (UDP/69) provides unauthenticated file read/write with no credential barrier. IPMI (UDP/623) exposes a critical CVE-2013-4786 RAKP hash-capture flaw enabling offline credential brute-force. NTP (UDP/123) leaks internal client IPs via monlist and is vulnerable to RCE if running ntpd < 4.2.8p3. RIP (UDP/520) allows unauthenticated route injection for traffic hijacking. No web services are present, eliminating web-based initial access vectors entirely. The most probable attack path is: SNMP community string brute-force for initial reconnaissance and MIB data collection, followed by IPMI hash capture for credential access, TFTP arbitrary file read for sensitive data exfiltration or file write for persistence, and rsyslog heap overflow for potential RCE if the service is genuinely listening.
